REPORT
Date August 12, 1938

FURTHER TO :-
Subject ASSISTANCE RENDERED TO JAPANESE MILITARY POLICE.

Made by D.S.I. Konovaloff Forwarded by D.I. Glover

Sir,

In view of the fact that no evidence has been found to substantiate the allegations made by the Japanese Military Police against the detained man Chang Dong (張桐), the undersigned requested Sgt. S. Tokutani to produce the informer for the purpose of questioning him regarding the source of information obtained by him.

On the morning of the 8th August 1938, Sgt. S. Tokutani, instead of bringing the informer, handed to the undersigned an anonymous letter written in Chinese, a copy and translation of which are attached herewith. Sgt. Tokutani further added that the Japanese Military Police had acted on the strength of this letter and that no informer was employed in this case. Sgt. Tokutani has also stated that upon the completion of an investigation the detained man Chang Dong can be released. The anonymous letter was submitted for examination to Cler. Asst. May Yoh, who had compared the handwriting of the letter with those on file but found to have no previous record.

On the 10th of August 1938 p.m., D.I. Wong Zung Ying and the undersigned together with the arrested man Chang Dong, visited addresses mentioned in the previous report. In each address the tenants on the premises have identified Chang Dong as the person who had resided therein during the mentioned period.

On being questioned in regard the identity of the author of the letter, "Lee Tsau" (李釗), the arrested man Chang Dong claimed no knowledge of the person by the name of Lee Tsau or any other persons who could have written this letter.

（左侧手写批注：S/Y, 3/8, 13/8）

报告
日期：1938年8月12日

续前件：-
事由：向日本宪兵队提供协助。

由副督察长科诺瓦洛夫（Konovaloff）呈报，经督察长格洛弗（Glover）转呈

先生：

鉴于未发现任何证据证实日本宪兵队对被拘留人张桐（Chang Dong）提出的指控，具名者要求佐藤谷（S. Tokutani）警士带出线人，以便就其获取情报的来源对其进行讯问。

1938年8月8日上午，佐藤谷警士并未带出线人，而是向具名者递交了一封中文匿名信，其副本及译文附后。佐藤谷警士还补充说，日本宪兵队是依据这封信采取行动的，在此案中并未雇用线人。佐藤谷警士还表示，调查结束后即可释放被拘留人张桐。该匿名信已提交给助理员梅约（May Yoh）进行审查，他将信中的笔迹与存档笔迹进行了比对，但未发现既往记录。

1938年8月10日下午，王宗英（Wong Zung Ying）督察与具名者一同，带着被捕人张桐，走访了前一份报告中提到的地址。在每个地址，住户均指认张桐为在上述期间居住于此的人。

当就被问及信件作者“李钊”（Lee Tsau）的身份时，被捕人张桐声称不认识名叫李钊的人，也不认识其他可能撰写此信的人。

（左侧手写批注：S/Y, 3/8, 13/8）

TRANSLATION OF A LETTER.

Mr. Ma,

I am one of the men who are extremely opposing the Bolshevicism and Chiang's Government. I honestly take the oath to the effect that I am willing to exert my-self under the "Reformed Government".

I was formerly working with the Central Branch of the Koumingtang Party, and had been despatched to various provinces to join the services of clearing Communists for several years.

I was later transferred to the Special District of Shanghai Municipality, where I participated the "Secret Service" of Oppressing the C.P. work, and attached to the "Special Service Branch" of the former Public Safety Bureau.

As a result of the National Government publicly accommodating the evil communists, therefore causing this terrible hostility, I started to work as a labourer in a factory in order to maintain my livelihood.

I am now in possession of the information that the ex-Chief of P.S.B., Tsai Chin Gan, is detailing some one to come to Shanghai with the instructions to have the P.S.B. documents which were left in Shanghai during the retreat of the Chinese troops, removed to Hankow.

I, therefore, respectfully submitted to you this information, and hope you will confiscate these documents for the purpose of your perusal. According to the man, sent here, the documents, contained in a case, were concealed beneath the floor. However, I am not positive that whether the case was hidden under the floor of the house of his friend, where he is living at present, or otherwise at
pages.zh:
信件译文。

马先生：

我是极力反对布尔什维主义和蒋介石政府的人士之一。我诚恳地宣誓，愿意在“维新政府”下效力。

我此前曾在国民党党部中央分部工作，并被派往各省从事清共工作数年。

后来我被调至上海特别市，参与镇压共产党工作的“特务”活动，隶属于前公安局的“特种勤务分支”。

由于国民政府公开容纳邪恶的共产党人，导致这种可怕的敌对状态，我为了维持生计，开始在一家工厂做工。

我现在掌握的情报是，前公安局局长蔡金根（Tsai Chin Gan）正派遣某人携带指令来到上海，旨在将中国军队撤退时留在上海的公安局文件转移至汉口。

因此，我谨向您提交此情报，希望您没收这些文件以供查阅。据被派来的人称，装文件的箱子藏在地板下面。然而，我不确定箱子是藏在他目前居住的朋友家的地板下，还是藏在

for Hongkong on the 5th inst., as he has booked a ticket

plain clothes men to search and confiscate the above
mentioned documents.

(Sd) Lee Tsau.
Date:- 3.8.38.

Sir,
At 11.10 p.m. on the 6th August 1938 D.S.I. Umemoto telephoned the undersigned, stating that the Japanese Military Police had requested the S.M.Police to render assistance in effecting the arrest of one terrorist and searching a house, at 1 a.m. the 7th August 1938. This request was immediately reported to Officer i/c C.l., D.I. Glover.
At 12.50 a.m. the 7.8.38 Sergeant S. Tokutani and three other members of the Japanese Military Police came to C.l. office and requested that the necessary assistance be now rendered. On being questioned Sergt. S. Tokutani stated that according to information obtained by an informer employed by the Japanese Military Police, one named Chang Dong (張桐) has recently arrived from Hankow with messages to be delivered to the terrorists operating in Shanghai. Sergeant S. Tokutani further added that the alleged messenger, Chang Dong, was to leave Shanghai and proceed back to Hankow this morning, the 7th August 1938, via the Hongkong Colony; and that a written message is to be conveyed by him to Hankow and which could be found in his possession. The address of the alleged messenger, Chang Dong, was given as 33 Woo Ling Terrace, Gordon Road.
On these informations being reported to D.I. Glover and instructions received D.S.I. Konovaloff, D.I. Wong and C.D.S. 304, and D.S. Mitsushima of the S.P.Office, accompanied by the Japanese Military Police, proceeded to Gordon Road Station, where the necessary assistance was obtained.

日期：1938年8月7日。
事由：向日本宪兵队提供协助。
由副督察长科诺瓦洛夫（KONOVALOFF）呈报，经督察长格洛弗（GLOVER）转呈。

先生：
1938年8月6日晚上11点10分，梅本（Umemoto）副督察长致电具名者，称日本宪兵队请求上海公共租界警务处提供协助，于1938年8月7日凌晨1点逮捕一名恐怖分子并搜查一处房屋。此请求立即报告给了中央捕房负责人、督察长格洛弗。
1938年8月7日凌晨12点50分，佐藤谷（S. Tokutani）警士及其他三名日本宪兵队成员来到中央捕房办公室，请求立即提供必要协助。经询问，佐藤谷警士称，根据日本宪兵队雇用的线人获得的情报，一名叫张桐（Chang Dong）的人最近从汉口抵达，带有要交付给在上海活动的恐怖分子的口信。佐藤谷警士还补充说，据称信使张桐将于今天早晨，即1938年8月7日，经由香港殖民地离开上海返回汉口；并且他将向汉口传递书面信息，该信息可在其身上找到。据称信使张桐的地址为戈登路武林里33号。

将这些情报报告给格洛弗督察并收到指示后，副督察长科诺瓦洛夫、王督察、刑事侦缉处304号警员以及特别办公室的三岛（Mitsushima）副警司，在日本宪兵队的陪同下，前往戈登路分站，在那里获得了必要的协助。

The given address was located in Lane 516, House Z 33
Gordon Road, just opposite the Police Station. The premises
in question is a Chinese dwelling house, occupied by twelve
different families. In a rear room, on the first floor the
alleged messenger, Chang Dong 張軔 alias Chang Tsong
Ping 張仲彬, age 35, native of Soochow, M/Unemployed, re-
siding at the above address, was found lying in the bed to-
gether with his wife, named Shih Hwei Ying (徐惠英). A
thorough search of the room was carried out, but no evidence
i.e. any written messages or letters of the political nature,
was found. Upon the request being made by Sergeant S. Tokutani,
the adjoining two rooms also were searched, but, likewise,
with negative results. However, Sgt. S. Tokutani requested
that the arrested person Chang Dong be taken to C.B.H.Q. and
detained pending further enquiries being made.

On being conveyed to C.I. offices and questioned by the
undersigned and D.I. Wong, the arrested man, Chang Dong pleaded
all ignorance of any messages were being conveyed by him to
Han-kow from Shanghai or vice-versa and he emphatically denied
having ever taken part in any political or terroristic activi-
ties.

However, Chang Dong admitted that on the 15th April 1938,
he proceeded to Hongkong on the S.S. "Chang Yuen (慶元)"
of B. & S. Steam Ship Company for the purpose of securing some
job through his friend named Sung Zau Yao (陳兆姚) who owns
in the colony a food-shop. Failing to obtain any employment
in Hongkong the arrested man Chang Dong returned to Shanghai
on the S.S. "Ang Ching (安慶)", of the B. & S. Company,

事由........................................................................
....................................................................................................
呈报人............................转呈人....................................................

所提供的地址位于戈登路516弄Z字33号，就在警察局对面。涉案房屋是一栋中式住宅，由十二个不同的家庭居住。在一楼的后房间里，发现了据称的信使张桐（Chang Dong，中文名张軔，别名张仲彬 Chang Tsong Ping），35岁，苏州人，职业：无业，居住于上述地址，他正与其妻子徐惠英（Shih Hwei Ying）躺在床上。对该房间进行了彻底搜查，但未发现任何证据，即任何具有政治性质的书面口信或信件。应佐藤谷警士的要求，相邻的两个房间也进行了搜查，但同样一无所获。然而，佐藤谷警士要求将被捕人张桐带至中央捕房总部予以拘留，以待进一步调查。

在被送往中央捕房办公室并由具名者和王督察讯问时，被捕人张桐辩称对任何从上海传往汉口或反之的口信一概不知，并坚决否认曾参与任何政治或恐怖活动。

然而，张桐承认，1938年4月15日，他乘坐宝顺轮船公司（B. & S. Steam Ship Company）的“庆元”轮（Chang Yuen）前往香港，目的是通过他在该殖民地拥有一家食品店的朋友陈兆姚（Sung Zau Yao）寻找工作。因未能在香港找到工作，被捕人张桐乘坐宝顺公司的“安庆”轮（Ang Ching）返回上海，

on the 24th June 1938 and since has been living at the present
address.

    At the time of conducting enquiries on the premises Chang
Dong's room mate, a male Chinese named Sung Hung Ching (陳鴻欽)
who is a partner of a Japanese, named T. Tomida, in wool and
cotton trading, and who is in possession of a Japanese pass
issued by the Japanese Consulate Police Authorising him to
enter the Northern area, corroborated the arrested man's statement
that he, Chang Dong, has not been absent from Shanghai since
his return from Hongkong, i.e. the 24th June 1938.

    Prior to the outbreak of hostilities in Shanghai the
arrested man, Chang Dong, was employed as a private assistant
to a clerk, named Zung Kyung Sung (陳重吉) at the Sinza Sub-
Station of the Chapei Police.

    After the retreat of the Chinese Army from the Shanghai
area, the arrested man, Chang Dong, took refuge in the Inter-
national Settlement at House 13, Tsang Ziang Li off Connaught
Road, on the 5.8.37. On the 27.9.37 he removed to House, No.2
Nyi Ying Faung, off Route de Conty, French Concession, and
vacated this address on the 27.11.37 and put up his residence
at the present address, House 33 Z Lane 516 Gordon Road.

    The arrested man, Chang Dong, is now being detained in
C.I. offices, pending further enquiries to be made, details
of which will be the subject of the next report.

Geo. B. Deyou.                I am, Sir,
8.6.38.
                              Yours obediently,

                              P. Konovaloff.
                              D. S. I.

                                    - 3 -
于1938年6月24日抵达，此后一直居住在现址。

    在对住所进行调查时，张桐的室友，一名叫陈鸿钦（Sung Hung Ching）的中国男子，证实了被捕人的陈述，即张桐自1938年6月24日从香港返回后未曾离开过上海。陈鸿钦是与日本人T. Tomida合伙从事羊毛和棉花贸易的商人，并持有日本领事馆警察签发的允许其进入北区的通行证。

    在上海战事爆发前，被捕人张桐受雇于闸北警察署新亚分站，担任一名叫陈重吉（Zung Kyung Sung）的文书的私人助理。

    在中国军队从上海地区撤退后，被捕人张桐于1937年8月5日避难至康纳脱路（Connaught Road）旁藏祥里13号的国际租界内。1937年9月27日，他搬至法租界康悌路（Route de Conty）旁倪英坊2号，并于1937年11月27日搬离该址，入住现址，即戈登路516弄Z字33号。

    被捕人张桐目前被拘押在中央捕房办公室，等待进一步调查，详情将在下一份报告中陈述。

Geo. B. Deyou.                此致，
1938年8月6日。
                              敬礼，

                              P. 科诺瓦洛夫。
                              副督察长。
